* ``*``
  Zero or more characters, none of which may be ``/``.  There is no
  ``**``: a run of stars behaves like a single star.
* ``?``
  Exactly one character, which may not be ``/``.
* ``[...]``
  One character from the set; ``[!...]`` matches one character NOT in
  the set.  Inside a set, ``-`` between two characters denotes a range

  out of ordinal order matches nothing.  A set is not restricted from
  matching ``/`` -- only ``*`` and ``?`` are.

  ``*``).  A lone trailing ``\\`` is an invalid pattern.

def matches(pattern, name):
    """Return ``True`` if the whole ``name`` matches the glob ``pattern``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: if ``pattern`` or ``name`` is not a ``str``.
        ValueError: if the pattern is invalid (unterminated ``[`` or a
            lone trailing ``\\``).
    """
    if not isinstance(pattern, str):
        raise TypeError(
            "pattern must be a str, got %s" % type(pattern).__name__

    if not isinstance(name, str):

        ("any",)                      -- ``?``
        ("lit", ch)                   -- one literal character
        ("set", chars, ranges, neg)   -- one char from (chars | ranges),

                                         chars is a frozenset[str],

    i = 0
    n = len(pattern)

            tokens.append(("any",))
